reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports that the laser method produces homogeneous, ultrafine HENAs and that slow kinetics cause segregation, but it provides no evidence regarding the high-temperature stability of the kinetically trapped state or its ability to suppress diffusion-driven segregation, which is the core mechanistic premise.
premises: Laser-induced thermionic emission reduction is a fast synthesis method that produces homogeneous HENAs.
Fast synthesis can kinetically trap a metastable, well-mixed atomic configuration.
Slow synthesis methods lead to phase segregation due to slow reaction kinetics.
The kinetically trapped state suppresses diffusion-driven phase segregation at high temperatures.
The defective carbon support stabilizes the nanoalloys and limits atom mobility.
